Group 3 — Bodies and talk

Studio wall

Author

Group names here

Spine

How do bodies measure, how do people talk about mind and school, and how long do countries live?

This sentence stays at the top. Every panel must attach to it. If a plot cannot be introduced in a clause that hangs off this line, it is off the wall.

Introduction — the tables we own

This folder is ours for the ten days. Three tables, three shapes.

  • Panel A (panel-A.csv) — body measures (bdims): height, weight, waist, hip, chest, age, sex. Stand-in for NHANES when that package is not on the machine.
  • Panel B (panel-B.csv) — GSS 2010: degree, grass, hours of work and rest. mntlhlth is days of poor mental health — a Quant. Do not mosaic it.
  • Panel C (panel-C.csv) — gapminder 2007: life expectancy, GDP per capita, population by country.

Found tables train the mark. A campus Free Hunch, if we collect one, is a made panel of the same pair type — new people, old grammar. It does not replace A, B, or C.

6. Say

We all found the density graph comparing chest sizes of men and women interesting because according to the graph, men have a bigger chest size than women which is quite unexpected. Men also have larger variation in the sizes while women have more difference in density for different sizes. This is surprising because according to the bar graph, the ratio of women is slightly more than men, in comparison. We also found the density graph comparing hip size of men and women surprising because it is contrasting the general belief that women have wider hips.

library(leaflet)

panel d — erin brokowich

In Erin Brockovich (2000), what starts off as a small investigation turns into something much bigger, exposing how a corporation has been poisoning an entire community. While working at a law firm, Erin comes across medical records that connect the residents of Hinkley, California, to the hexavalent chromium contamination caused by PG&E.

This map looks at the places and people involved in the case. The PG&E facility shows where the contamination originated, while the highlighted groundwater area and the expanding plume show how the pollution spread beyond the company’s property. The outlined area represents the affected community, and the markers point out some of the residents whose lives became part of Erin’s investigation.

The locations of Donna Jensen, Pete Goya and Roberta Walker help connect the map to the actual people behind the case. Through Erin’s visits to their homes, we get to see the human side of the investigation. It is no longer just about medical records or corporate documents, but about the fear, illness and uncertainty that these families had to live with.

What I find interesting is how a map of a small desert town can become a way of showing accountability. By putting the facility, the contamination and the residents together in one landscape, the map shows how the story is not just about where the pollution came from, but about the people whose lives were affected by it.

# Spine

> How do bodies measure, how do people talk about mind and school, and how long do countries live?

This sentence stays at the top. Every panel must attach to it. If a plot cannot be introduced in a clause that hangs off this line, it is off the wall.

# Introduction — the tables we own

This folder is ours for the ten days. Three tables, three shapes.

- **Panel A** (`panel-A.csv`) — body measures (`bdims`): height, weight, waist, hip, chest, age, sex. Stand-in for NHANES when that package is not on the machine.
- **Panel B** (`panel-B.csv`) — GSS 2010: `degree`, `grass`, hours of work and rest. `mntlhlth` is *days* of poor mental health — a Quant. Do not mosaic it.
- **Panel C** (`panel-C.csv`) — gapminder 2007: life expectancy, GDP per capita, population by country.

Found tables train the mark. A campus Free Hunch, if we collect one, is a **made** panel of the same pair type — new people, old grammar. It does not replace A, B, or C.

{{< include _setup.qmd >}}

We all found the density graph comparing chest sizes of men and women interesting because according to the graph, men have a bigger chest size than women which is quite unexpected. Men also have larger variation in the sizes while women have more difference in density for different sizes. looking at the graph, the ratio of people who think marijuana should be legal and not Legal appears to be similar, in each individual degree. But this could also be because the number of high schoolers in this dataset is much more.

# panel d — erin brokowich

In *Erin Brockovich* (2000), what starts off as a small investigation turns into something much bigger, exposing how a corporation has been poisoning an entire community. While working at a law firm, Erin comes across medical records that connect the residents of Hinkley, California, to the hexavalent chromium contamination caused by PG&E.

This map looks at the places and people involved in the case. The PG&E facility shows where the contamination originated, while the highlighted groundwater area and the expanding plume show how the pollution spread beyond the company's property. The outlined area represents the affected community, and the markers point out some of the residents whose lives became part of Erin's investigation.

The locations of Donna Jensen, Pete Goya and Roberta Walker help connect the map to the actual people behind the case. Through Erin's visits to their homes, we get to see the human side of the investigation. It is no longer just about medical records or corporate documents, but about the fear, illness and uncertainty that these families had to live with.

What I find interesting is how a map of a small desert town can become a way of showing accountability. By putting the facility, the contamination and the residents together in one landscape, the map shows how the story is not just about where the pollution came from, but about the people whose lives were affected by it.
